reuse.why: Most consumers share getExpectedAmount and reuse getApproxNumberThreshold, but getScheduledAmount retains a parallel amount resolver.

duplication.why: Missing-value and numeric-versus-range dispatch remains duplicated in getScheduledAmount and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions.

placement.why: Schedule amount policy belongs in shared/schedules, tolerance remains in shared/rules, and API serialization stays in api-models.

scope.why: The changes are confined to schedule amount policy, its consumers, API types, tests, and release notes.

maintainability.why: The central helper simplifies most consumers, but parallel resolution paths and outdated policy comments make future rule changes harder to maintain.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts: getScheduledAmount bypasses getExpectedAmount, while computeSchedulePreviewTransactions retains local missing/numeric dispatch before calling it.

disguised_duplication.where: packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts: getScheduledAmount expresses the same missing/numeric/range dispatch as getExpectedAmount using early returns and inversion, while computeSchedulePreviewTransactions retains it as nested ternaries.

abstraction_drift.where: getExpectedAmount gains the op parameter and an isapprox branch, but getScheduledAmount and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions retain independent dispatch instead of delegating the entire decision.
